ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Propaganda by Pakistan on Kashmir 
*101. SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH LIBRA: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Pakistan has directed militant outfits to set 
up offices in major cities around the world to spread propaganda about 
Kashmir, as reported in the Times of India, dated 7th February, 2000; 
(b) whether Pakistan's ISI has also directed all militant groups 
operating in Jammu and Kashmir to intensify their activ ities in view of US 
President's ensuing visit to India; and 
(c) if so, the reaction of Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT 
SINGH): (a) to (c) Government have seen the report appearing in the "Times 
of India", on 7th January 2000.  Pakistan continues to pursue activities 
directed at spreading propaganda about Jammu and Kashmir in the 
international community. Its sponsorship of cross border terrorism in the 
State of Jammu and Kashmir and elsewhere in India also continues unabated. 
Government have appropriately and effectively been bringing to the notice 
of the international community. Pakistan's support to cross border terrorism 
and hostile anti -India propaganda. The international community now openly 
recognizes Pakistan's state spons orship of terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir 
and elsewhere in India. This is being reflected in the statements by official 
spokesmen of several foreign governments and in the international media 
coverage of Pakistan.

Government continue to take all measures necessary to preserve the 
security and territorial integrity of the country.

SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Sir, the hon. Minister in the later part of 
his statement, in reply to parts (a) and (c) has stated, 'The international 
community now openly recognizes Pakistan's state sponsorship of terrorism 
in Jammu and Kashmir and elsewhere in India.' I would like to know how 
many countries ha ve openly stated that Pakistan is sponsoring terrorism in 
Jammu and Kashmir. In this connection, I would also like know —apart from 
the comments in the newspapers—in which international fora, these countries 
have expressed their view that Pakistan is indulging in cross -border terrorism 
in Jammu and Kashmir. I would also like to know from the hon. Minister as to 
what has been the response to the appeal made by the Government of India or 
to the suggestions made by the Government of India to declare Pakistan as  a 
terrorist State. I have read in the newspapers about the observations made by 
the Prime Minister. But I would like to know whether any country has 
reponded to this suggestion of the Government of India, and if so, which are 
those countries. 
SHRI JASWANT  SINGH: Mr. Chairman, Sir so, far as listing the 
countries that have tacitly, implicitly, by action and by statements, recognised 
that there now exists an unacceptable level of encouragement by the State or 
the agencies of the State of Pakistan to terroris m, it can be cited to the hon. 
Member, but the problem is that in citing the countries now, I might miss out 
one or two names. So, I will send the information directly to him. So far as 
the international fora are concerned, I might remind the hon. Member t hat in 
the Indian Resolution on the UN Convention on Terrorism, it has received the 
widest possible support as never up till now. I might also remind the hon. 
Member that Agreements to work against international terrorism and the 
setting up of Joint Workin g Groups on terrorism is an index of the 
international recognition of the State of Pakistan supporting directly or 
through agencies of State, terrorism 

RAJYA SABHA [2nd March, 2000] 
in the Indian State of Jammu and Kashmir. And regarding the final part of  the 
question relating to an appeal, may I point out to the hon. Member that India 
does not make appeals? India makes its views known, and India has made 
known its veiws about treating Pakistan as a sponsor of State terrorism. This 
is not the first time th at it has been made. It has also been made earlier and, 
today, there is a much greater recognition of the sponsorship of terrorism by 
Pakistan than ever earlier. 
SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: 'Sir, I am not at all happy with the 
response of the hon. Minister. The hon. Minister has categorically stated in the 
statement, "the international community now openly recognizes." Therefore, 
the Minister must be in the possession of the list of the countries, at least, 
some of the names. You give me some illustrative list. Otherwise, why are you 
making this statement that the international community now openly recognizes 
Pakistan's state sponsorship of terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir? He has very 
cleverly avoided the second point. "We expressed our opinion and we 
expressed our views also." That is why, I have suggested, 'not only appeal,' 
but I have used the word 'suggestions' also. The international communities 
have responded to that and, surely, the MEA is fully aware of it. Therefore, 
there is no point in saying, in general  terms, that it is being world -recognized. 
Has the USA responded to these views of the Government of India in a 
particular way? I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether the 
United Kingdom or any other P -5 country has responded to this view of th e 
Government of India in any particular way. 
SHRI JASWANT SINGH: So far as listing the countries, and more directly 
about the USA and P -5 countries, is concerned, I would like to say that on 
several occasions, repeatedly, Russia has already publicly given a statement 
to the fact that pakistan is a sponsor of terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir and 
elsewhere, (a) The United States of America is establishing a Joint Working 
Group on terrorism, (b) On a commitment to work with India. It is a public 
commitment that the United States of America shall work with India and co -
operate in all respects to apprehend the hijackers who have sought shelter in 
Pakistan. The United States of America has given its views publicly to that 
effect. On the 27th of January, the US State

Minister not to rely too much on the Americans to s olve the Kashmii  
issue. 
Another aspect, which I am raising, is this. Now, the security  
situation is much worse than what it was before the Pokhrar  
explosion. There is military regime in Pakistan. They have nucleai  
power. The distance between America and Ru ssia is far more than  
the distance between Pakistan and India. It will take only three  
minutes for a missile to reach Delhi from Pakistan. So, the situation

RAJYA SABHA [2nd March, 2000] 
is much more serious. There is a very serious situation. In that c ontext, what 
is the Government proposing to do to work out some procedure? Given this 
antagonism, there should be some procedure to ensure that there is some 
check on any missile threat and all that, before any counter -action is taken 
from both sides. I would like to know whether any procedure has been laid 
down to ensure our security against any nuclear attack. 
SHRI JASWANT SINGH: Sir, the hon. Member has put two question. 
Both are of significance. The second question really doesn't arise from the 
main question that has been put today. But, nevertheless, considering the deep 
import of it, may I assure the hon. Member that so far as the Government is 
concerned, on the totality of the nuclear doctrine as also the mechanism, that 
remains to be adopted by the G overnment to safeguard our security against 
the kind of contingencies or possibilities that may arise, please be assured that 
all this has been done. At an appropriate moment when a discussion takes 
place in this House, no doubt a great deal of it, then we will exchange ideas 
and information between the hon. Members and the House, subject, of course, 
to security and other aspects which the hon. Member has recognised. So far as 
the first part of the qustion is concerned, I assure the hon. Member that the 
Government is not approaching the task of working out new modus vivendi 
with the United States of America. After the experience of the past fifty years, 
we recognise that the United States of America has its geo -strategic and 
political compulsions relating to  South Asia. They have invested in the past 
five decades in a certain kind of a balance or equation in the South Asain sub -
continent. It has cen our endeavour to bring the United States of America to 
the post cold -war position and to recognise the new real ity. I also assure the 
hon. Member that we are approaching this task fully conscious of all the 
lessons of history. But I might disabuse you of the notion thal the United 
States of America, through some subterfuge, inadvertently, or that because the 
Government is caught on the wrong foot, might introduce itself as a kind of an 
agent in the issue of the Indian State of Jammu & Kashmir. Please rest 
assured, it won't be. Indeed, in the UN General Assembly, for the first time 
ever—after the hon. Prime Minister clarified, that I should say so —I made 
explicit to the UN General 
6 

[2nd March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
        Assembly that the Indian State of Jammu and Kashmir is not the so -called 
core issue between India and Pakistan. It is at the core of the Indian 
nationhood; and that was in a publicly stated statement in the UN General 
Assembly—let there be no ambiguity or doubt in your mind that the United 
States of America or any other country, for that matter in the world, through 
any mechanism, covert or overt, shal l be able to introduce themselves into 
this area. . 
DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: Sir, I would like to know whether the 
Government is aware of the Pak terrorist activities in various parts of the 
country, specially in South. In Hyderabad, recently, four Pak nati onals were 
arrested with fake notes. This activity is being spread specially in Hyderabad 
and Nizamabad districts. I believe through police sources that there are six 
thousand pak nationals whose visas have expired. And still they are staying in 
those part s. I would like to know from the hon. Minister what action the 
Government is taking in this regard. 
SHRI JASWANT SINGH: Sir, actually the question of the hon. Member 
consists of three parts. One relates to fake currency which has been answered 
earlier. The Government is very mindful of it. I should say that it is seized of 
this issue. Indeed, I might say that the hon. Prime Minister himself has shared 
his concern, in this regard, with me personally. There are two other aspects of 
the question. One relates t o extension of ISI activities in the Southern States. 
Sir, it is not strictly within the folds of the Ministry of External Affairs. But I 
am duty bound to inform the hon. Member that the Government is fully 
seized of this issue. The Home Ministry is alert on the subject and I can 
assure the hon. Member that much greater attention is being paid to this now 
than ever, or earlier. The third question, without doubt, is a serious question. 
He said that about six thousand visa holders who came from Western 
neighbouring country, Pakistan, are now not traceable. This is a phenomenon 
that we have been experiencing for the past many years. It is one of the 
difficulties we have been facing because of the very nature of the two lands 
and of the population. Sir, readily,  I have not with me the numbers of visa 
holders who came to India and simply evaporated or melted within the larger 
milieu of India. That is one part of the problem. The other part of the problem 
is this. Visa holders coming and melting into 
7

*116. SHRI C.P. THIRUNAVUKKARASU:  
 SHRI V.P. DURAISAMY: 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that some Tamil Nadu fishermen have been 
lodged in Pakistani jails since June, 1999; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that they have been handed over to 
Pakistani' authorities by the Iranian Government; 
(c) what diplomatic efforts have been made, so far, by Government to 
get them released; and

exchange of Pakistani fishermen who were caught, recently in the Gujarat 
coast? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT 
SINGH): (a) to (d) On receipt of information that 19 fishermen belonging to 
Tamil Nadu were in Pakistan custody, Government raised the matter in July 
1999 with the Government of Pakistan and demanded that they be released 
immediately so that they could be repatriated to India. It was also learnt that 
these fishermen had gone to Saudi Arabia but, while fishing, had strayed into 
Iranian territorial waters, following which Iranian authorities pushed them 
into Pakistan. This matter was taken up with the Iranian authorities through 
diplomatic channels on several occasions. They have assured that such 
incidents would not be repeated in future. 
After repeated reminders by Government, the Government of Pakistan 
acknowledged the presence in its custody of the 19 fishermen in September 
1999. Consular access to these fishermen was provided only on 3 January, 
2000. Since then, Pakistani authorities have not indicated their willingness to 
release the detained fishermen. Discus sions for the release of fishermen of 
both countries in each others custody continue through diplomatic channels.

829. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of LABOUR be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether ESIC has any long term objective with regard to attending 
to medical problems of workers, who are insured persons; 
(b) if so, what are these objectives; 
(c) whether there is any proposal to build large super speciality hospitals 
in some key States by ESIC; 
(d) to what extent has ESIC fulfilled the objectives of attending to all the 
medical requirements of insured persons;

and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI MUNI LALL): (a) to (f) The objective of the ESI 
Scheme has been and continues to be to provide certain cash benefits namely the 
sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disablement benefit, dependent benefit and to 
provide for medical care to the insured persons (IPs) and their families. Under 
Section 58 of the ESI Act, it is the responsibility of the State Governments to 
provide for insured persons reasonable medical, surgical and obstetric 
treatment. Accordingly medical care is being 
124 

[2nd March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
administered by the State Governments and U.T. Administrations except in 
Delhi and NOIDA where it is being administered directly by the ESIC. 
With a view to achieving its objectives, the ESI Corporation has already 
set up 137 ESI hospitals, 43 annexes and 1452 dispensaries in the 
implemented areas for providing medical care to the insured persons and 
their families. Besides reserving 3519 beds in other hospitals, the 
Corporation has also set up 2722 IMP clinics. The latest super -speciality 
services are presently being made available to the beneficiaries through tie -
up arrangements with reputed medical institutions. A Revolving Fund has 
also been constituted by the ESIC for providing advances for super speciality 
tests and treatment. 
Review of functioning of the ESIC is an on- going process and change in 
operation of the scheme is made as and when considered necessary. R ecently, 
on the basis of recommendations of the Satyam Committee, ceiling on the 
expenditure on medical care has been enhanced by the ESIC from Rs. 500/ - 
to Rs. 600/ - per LP. per annum with effect from 1.4.99. In order to improve 
medical care facilities in  ESI hospitals/dispensaries, the ESIC Corporation 
has recently formulated an Action Plan and forwarded the same to the State 
Governments for implementation in consultation with ESI Corporation. The 
Action Plan includes, inter-alia, provision of modern equi pments in hospitals, 
establishment of Regional trauma centres, establisment of super -speciality 
services, blood banks, cancer prevention centres, development of indigenous 
system of medicine, provision of necessary equipments in dispensaries etc. In 
order to provide proper diagnosis and timely treatment of occupational 
diseases, the Corporation has set up four Occupational Diseases Centres i.e. 
one each at Delhi Calcutta, Mumbai and Chennai and expenditure on running

recommendations of ILO so far not being ratified by India;

ILO recommendations are being followed at enterprise level; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT (SHRI MUNI LALL): (a) to (c) There are 182 ILO 
Conventions and 190 ILO Recommendations treated as international labour 
standards, Conventions are open to ratification by member States whereas 
Recommendations are guidelines to member countries. India has ratified 38

compared to even many developed countries. Out of the remaining 5 Core 
Conventions, the Government has decided to ratify Convention No. 105 
concerning abolition of forced labour and a statement to this effect will be 
laid before both the Houses of Parliament during this session. The

Statement 
Recommendations of Dr. Nitish Sengupta Committee Report 
On the basis of detailed study and assessment of various key success 
factors, the Committee has evaluated and assessed the position of IBP, CRL, 
MRL, BRPL and NRL. The Committee has also carefully considered the 
likely status of BPC in the context of a completely deregulated scenario. 
Taking into consideration the evaluation and assessment carried out by 
the Committee, the  following recommendations have been made so as to 
ensure that all stand -alone oil companies become stronger in the deregulated 
market and also to create a fair and competitive market for enhancement of 
customer services: 
(a) BPC should buy up the entire shareholding of Govt. of India in CRL 
and make CRL its subsidiary. The marketing arrangement, if any, 
with IOC should accordingly be modified. 
(b) Though at present IOC is a strong candidate for an alliance with 
MRL, the Committee recommends that for the time being  the 
marketing arrangement of MRL with IOC should continue. Since, 
IOC is already a dominant player and as it is necessary to ensure 
fair competition, the Committee suggests that BPC be also 
considered in the intermediate future as a serious candidate 
alongwith IOC to partner MRL. However, this should be done after 
about 18—24 months to allow BPC sufficient time to stabilise after 
its takeover of CRL and the demonstration of its ability to do so 
without affecting the supply line and its recommended investme nt 
in IBP. 
159 

RAJYA SABHA [2nd March, 2000] 
(c) IOC should buy up the entire shareholding of Govt of India in BRPL 
and make this company its subsidiary. 
(d) NRL should continue with BPC and IBP who are the majority 
shareholders along with Government of Assam. However, the Committee 
recommends that OIL should be roped in as a shareholder with 10% 
share, which can be allotted to them on preferential allotment basis out 
of the shares earmarked for public issue thereby creating an 
integrated oil net work in the North  East. This process will also 
enhance the sen timent of the prospective investors in the capital 
market for purposes of its ensuing public issue. 
(e) The Committee recommends that IBP should continue as a separate 
corporate entity for the time being. However, i t feels that IBP needs 
a strong strategic partner for continued supply of products and also 
providing marketing back up and necessary financial support. 
Accordingly, it endorses the views of the Disinvestment 
Commission that Government of India should disi nvest 33.58% in 
favour of a strategic partner. After careful study and consideration 
at various strategic alliance options, based on various success 
factors, the Committee feels that BPC is a strong candidate in 
comparison to other oil companies. Therefore, Government of India 
should disinvest its shareholdings in IBP in excess of 26% in favour 
of BPC as permissible under the SEBI take over guidelines. If these 
guidelines stand in the way of one shot of acquisition of this block of 
shareholding by BPC, this  may have to be done in phases or a 
portion of the shareholding now held by financial institutions may 
have to be transferred to BPC. 
(f) IBP should be assured of the required products from Mathura and/or 
Panipat in the North and MRL and CRL in the South throu gh 
appropriate marketing tie- ups for a period of at least five years after 
the end of APM period in order to maintain its supplies. 
(g) Government of India should constitute a petroleum regulatory body 
in lieu of OCC, who should regulate the 
160 

[2nd March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
supply of products besides handing critical issues during the 
transition period of deregulation. 
(h) All the existing pipelines excluding strategic pipelines owned by IOC 
should be transferred to an independent company such as the 
Petronet India Limited so that all the marketing companies get fair 
and equitable access to these pipelines for movement of products. 
(i) After implementation of the recommendation, the Committee has 
identified that there will be three market players, e.g., IOC, H PC 
and BPC -IBP. It feels that at a later date, the possibility of a 
combination of HPC, BPC -IBP, CRL, MRL, and NRL should be 
explored through an umbrella of a holding company. This new 
entity will be equal in size to IOC and would not only provide good 
competition but could also emerge as a global player in competition 
with the international oil majors.

the Sixth Five Year Plan 
176 

[2nd March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
(1980-85), the Government has been implementing employment and asset 
generation schemes for the upliftment of the people living below the poverty 
line. These schemes are mainly of two types, self -employment and wage 
employment Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) has been the 
major self -employment programme and it has been in op eration in all the 
blocks of the country since 1980. The wage emplopyment programme initially 
was National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) during the Sixth Plan 
period. In the Seventh Plan, another wage employment programme under the 
name Rural Labour Em ployment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was 
intrpduced.Then in 1989, Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) was launched by 
merging the National Rural Employment Programme and the Rural Labour 
Employment Guarantee Programme, and it became the main wage-
employment programme. In addition, several programmes to help the poor 
were also in operation until March, 1999. These programmes are Million 
Wells Scheme (MWS), Employment Assurance Scheme (FAS), Development 
of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA), Training of Rural Youth 
for Self-Employment (TRYSEM), Supply of improved Toolkits to Rural 
Artisans (SITRA). 
From 1st April, 1999, IRDP and allied programmes along with Million 
Wells Scheme have been restructured into single self -employment 
programme called the Swaranajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) with 
the primary objectives of focussed approach to poverty alleviation, capitalising 
advantages of group lending, and overcoming the problems associated with 
multiplicity of programmes. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) has also been 
restructured as Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY) with the primary 
objective of creation of demand driven community village infrastructure 
including durable assets at the village level and assets to enable the rural poor 
to increase the opportunitie s for sustained employment. Its secondary 
objective is generation of supplementary employment for the unemployed 
poor in the rural areas. Employment Assurance Scheme has also been 
strengthened from 1st April, 1999 as single wage employment programme. 
The w age employment under the programme is given to Below Poverty 
Lines (BPL) families.

house, if any resident member of the family has annual income from 
salary/self-employment exceeding Rs. 20,000 per annum (Rs. 1,700 per 
month), or if the family possesses a Television set, Refrigerator, Ceiling Fan, 
Motor Cycle/Scooter, Three- Wheeler, or if the family owns a Tractor, Power 
Tiller, Combined Thresher/Harvester, then the family is excluded  from the 
BPL group. 
Among the remaining families, the total consumption, both purchased 
from the market and home grown, are divided by the total number of persons 
in the family. If this amount falls below the 
179 

RAJYA SABHA [2nd March, 2000] 
poverty line expenditure which is worked out at state level using the 
methodology contained in the report of the Expert Group on Estimation of 
Proportion and Number of Poor (Lakdawala Committee), then the family is 
considered to be declared in the poor group (BPL). 
(b) In the beginning of the Ninth Five Year Plan 1997-2002. 
(c) The number has not yet been finalised by the State Government. 
(d) Since the Sixth Five Year Plan (1980 — 85), the Government  
has been implementing employment and asset generation schemes for  
the upliftment of the people living below the poverty line. These  
schemes are mainly of two types, self -employment and wage  
employment. Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) has  
been the major self -employment programme and it has been in 
operation in all the blocks of the country since 1980. The wage  
employment programme initially was National Rural Employment  
Programme (NREP) during the Sixh Plan period, In the Seventh*  
Plan, another wage employment programmes under the name Rural  
Labour Employment Guarantee  Programme (RLEGP) was  
introduced. Then in 1989, Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) was  
launched by merging the Nationa l Rural Employment Programme  
and the Rural Labour Employment Guarantee Programme, and it  
became the main wage- employment programme. In addition, several  
programmes to help the poor were also in operation until March,  
1999. These programmes are Million Well s Scheme (MWS),  
Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS), Development of Women and  
Children in Rural Area (DWCRA), Training of Rural Youth for Self - 
Employment (TRYSEM), Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural  
Artisans (SITRA). 
From 1st April, 1999, IRDP and allied programmes, alongwith Million 
Wells Scheme have been restructured into, single self -employment 
programme called the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) with 
the primary objectives of focussed approach to poverty alleviation. Jawahar 
Rozgar Yojana (J RY) has also been restructured as Jawahar Gram Samridhi 
Yojana (JGSY) with the primary objective of creation of demand driven 
community village 
180 

[2nd March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
infrastructure including durable assets at the village level and assets to en able 
the rural poor to increase the opportunities for sustained employment. Its 
secondary objetive is generation of supplementary employment for the 
unemployed poor in the rural areas. Employment Assurance Scheme has also 
been strengthened from 1.4.1999 as single wage employment programme. The 
wage employment under the programme is given to Below Poverty Lines 
(BPL) families. 
From 1.12.1997, Swarna Jayanti Sahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) is the 
main poverty alleviation programme in the urban areas. The SJSRY, which 
has subsumed all the earlier three urban poverty alleviation programmes, 
viz., Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY), Urban Basic services for the Poor 
(UBSP), Prime Minister's Integrated Urban Poverty Eradication Programme 
(PMIUPEP), seeks to provide gainful em ployment to unemployed or 
underemployed urban and educated up to IX standard for setting up self 
employment ventures or provision of wage employment. The implementation 
of SJSRY is relying on suitable community structures on the UBSP pattern 
and delivery of inputs under this programme is through the medium of Urban 
Local Bodies (ULBs) and such community structure.

SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN (Kerala):Mr. Vice- Chairman I am 
grateful to you for having permitted me to raise an important issue before the 
House. 
The prices of milling copra and coconout have gone down very 
much during the past one or two months, especially, during the last two 
weeks. The Government of India used to declare a support price for milling 
copra year after year. unfortunately, for the year 2000, the Government of 
India has not so far declared a support price. There is an inordinate delay in 
declaring the support price. That is the main reason for the severe fall in 
prices of milling copra and coconut. As a result of that, lakhs of cultivators

financial loss and in the case of a majority of them, even sus tenance has 
become very difficult. Therefore, my request to the Government of India is 
that the Government of India should immediately come forward to declare a 
support price for milling copra for this year. That will not be enough. Along 
with that, while declaring the support price, necessary arrangements should be 
made to procure coconut at the support price. Normally, the NABARD is 
being entrusted with the job. The NABARD is being directed to make 
arrangement for procuring copra. It can be done this time also. Therefore, my 
request is that the support price should be declared immediately and 
necessary arrangements should be made  for procurement of coconut and 
milling  copra at the declared price.

Minorities Commission. The Commission's unhappiness with the steps taken

minorities. This is the thing.

not allow the circular of the Government of Gujarat to be implemented 
because the RSS is an organisation which according to us creates problems. 
That circular should be withdrawn. Thank you.

RSS and its activities and subsequently removing it. It has been argued that 
the RSS is not a political party. Therefore, the ban was not justified in the

their activities is liable to disciplinary action." Madam, in 1980, the 
Government again clarified and reiterated its decision not to permit civil 
servants to participate in the activitie s of the RSS and the jamat-e-islami. It
